answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works through a proof-of-escrow gate on identity: each new agent must post a bond slashed if it forks into lookalike identities. Reputation anchors to that stake, so an attacker cloning a thousand agents must fund a thousand separate bonds at full price, and detection burns them all at once. A shared registry acts as an atlas of bonded agents, letting honest peers cross-check a beacon of verified history before transacting, while the nadir of a fake swarm is that its cost scales with every added identity, never near zero.
